summary: Narrow RETEST of 3 issues from iteration_307. (1) Emily on New campaign with the 'press 1 to talk to sales' prompt now applies mode='transfer' with stopKey=9 and no campaign-flow errors — FIXED on both runs. (2) Quick-call 'Stop-calls key' dropdown now behaves as spec'd: every digit except active-keys, except the currently-selected stopKey stays visible even when added to activeKeys, and campaign-flow raises the expected 'both normal and stop-calls key' ERROR — FIXED. (3) IVR queue-callback / queue-announce checkboxes toggle correctly via real page.click (page.click, no set_checked) — the LOW-priority quirk from 307 is NOT reproducible and appears to have been a stale/flaky observation. One remaining defect: Scenario 2 (menu-mode request). Emily correctly picks mode='menu' with keys 1 & 2, but the script she writes still ends with 'Press 9 to stop these calls.' even though menu mode has no stopKey field, producing an ERROR in campaign-flow: 'message — The message promises that key 9 stops future calls, but no stop-calls key is set.' Task expected no stop-key promise in the script and no errors in menu mode.

ui_bugs.issue: For the 2-key menu prompt ('Press 1 for sales, press 2 for opening hours'), Emily correctly applies mode='Route each key (menu)' with 2 menu entries, but the script she generates contains the sentence 'Press 9 to stop these calls.' Since menu mode has no Keys-that-count / Stop-calls key fields, this produces a campaign-flow ERROR: 'message — The message promises that key 9 stops future calls, but no stop-calls key is set. Set the stop-calls key to 9, or remove that line.' Expected: no stop-key line in the script when Emily chooses menu mode (or add the stop line to the menu somehow). Reproducible on first attempt. Observed script: 'Hello, this is [Business name]. We have a weekend sale! Press 1 to talk to sales, or press 2 to hear our opening hours. Press 9 to stop these calls.'

action_items: Teach Emily's menu-mode prompt generator to NOT append a 'Press 9 to stop these calls.' sentence when mode='menu' (since the campaign has no stopKey field in that mode), OR drop that sentence from the final script when mode is menu. Current behaviour: script mentions stop-9 → flow validator raises ERROR.
critical_code_review_comments: Campaigns.js line 333 (unchanged observation): stopKey is already force-dropped when mode='menu' (`f.mode === 'menu' ? undefined : (f.stopKey || undefined)`). The complementary step — stripping any stop-key language from `script.text` when mode='menu' — is still missing. Either the assistant must stop writing that sentence, or the applier should strip it, otherwise the two intents keep conflicting whenever Emily hears 'stop' plus a menu request.

Scenario 3 passes end-to-end — the quick-call stop-key options are now derived dynamically (`['9'..'0'].filter(k => k === f.stopKey || !activeKeys.includes(k))`), which both hides the current activeKeys and keeps the current stopKey visible even when it conflicts. The validator then reports the conflict as an ERROR in quick-flow, as expected.

success_rate.frontend: ~92% — 3 of 4 scenarios pass; 1 (S2 menu-mode) still produces an error

The one remaining issue is S2: Emily writes 'Press 9 to stop these calls.' in the script even in menu mode. Keep the retest focused on that path; use prompt 'Weekend sale announcement. Press 1 for sales at +14155550100, press 2 to hear our opening hours...' and inspect `[data-testid="campaign-flow"]` for the 'message promises key 9' error.
